prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Should I prune or not?

Hello everyone, I need help with a bird of paradise. We’ve had this plant for about a year, we never cut any leaves or branch from it but we are debating whether or not we should start cutting some old/not so good looking leaves. We don’t know if it will help or harm our plant. Which one should we cut and why please? She recently made 2 new leaves (one from each “main branch”). Also any tips on maintenance would be appreciated. Thanks!

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: nothing is seriously wrong.** This looks like a healthy bird of paradise (probably *Strelitzia nicolai*) that is aging normally. The splits in the big leaves are natural, and wind and sun on a balcony make the outer leaves look ragged. Two new leaves coming up from the two main stems is a good sign.

**What to cut:** Remove only leaves that are mostly brown, dry, or yellow. Start with the oldest, lowest leaves, and cut the stalk (petiole) at its base, close to the soil line, with clean, sharp pruners. Leave any leaf that is still mostly green, even if it looks tattered, because it still feeds the plant. Don't remove more than about a third of the foliage at once. Those torn green leaves can stay.

**Maintenance:**
- **Light:** Keep it in the brightest spot you have. If you move it to a sunnier position, do it gradually over a week or two, or the leaves can scorch.
- **Watering:** Water thoroughly when the top 2–3 inches of soil are dry. Empty any water that collects in the decorative outer pot or saucer, and make sure the inner pot drains. Soggy roots are the most common way these plants decline.
- **Feeding:** Use a balanced liquid fertilizer every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer, and stop in fall and winter.
- **Temperature:** Bring it in before temperatures drop below about 50°F (10°C), since cold damages the leaves.
- **Repotting:** It is probably fine for now. Repot only when roots fill the pot, usually every 2–3 years, moving up one size.
- **Flowers:** Mature plants bloom with the orange-and-blue flowers when they are well established and get enough sun, so be patient.
